instructions: Compare the changed clause with the linked clause. Choose contradicts when the changed behavior conflicts with the target clause or its non-goal. Choose overlaps when both clauses describe the same behavior or surface. Choose oversteps when the changed clause adds a behavior beyond the target clause's stated boundary. Do not flag a merely related clause.

labels.name: contradicts
labels.description: The changed clause conflicts with the target clause or with a non-goal in the same spec.
examples: A draft adds automatic tracker writes while the same spec lists tracker changes as a non-goal.
A changed clause allows agent spool writes while the review boundary says only human clicks write events.

labels.name: overlaps
labels.description: The changed clause and target clause describe the same behavior, surface, or responsibility.
examples: A new suggestion clause restates a served spec's existing review-server behavior.
Two clauses both define the same cache key and record reuse rule.

labels.name: oversteps
labels.description: The changed clause extends beyond the target clause's stated scope or boundary without directly contradicting it.
examples: A clause expands a browser-only display rule into server-side provider policy.
A draft surface claims edits are automatic even though the target boundary permits only a human action.

labels.name: unrelated
labels.description: The changed clause and target clause share no behavior or boundary that needs a review flag.
examples: A changed cache sentence is compared with a clause about mobile layout and does not touch its behavior.
A new comment display label is compared with an unrelated Git baseline rule.

labels.name: unsure
labels.description: The relationship cannot be determined confidently from the two clauses and their supplied context.
examples: A terse changed clause and a broad target boundary use different terms with too little context to decide.
Two clauses mention review but provide no shared behavior or explicit boundary.
